Are you looking for a hands-on role where you can help keep our fleet safe, clean, and ready for service?

• Fueling buses as they return to the depot after service.

• Carrying out interior, exterior, engine bay, and under-chassis cleaning of company vehicles.
• Cleaning depot facilities, including offices, workshops, welfare areas, and other operational spaces.

• Carrying out regular checks on cleaning equipment, tools, and supplies.
• Following all Stagecoach safety policies and procedures to ensure a safe working environment.
What we're looking for
• A positive and reliable team player with a strong work ethic.
• Good communication and interpersonal skills.
• Previous experience in cleaning, vehicle presentation, facilities, logistics, or a similar operational environment would be advantageous.
• Excellent attention to detail and pride in maintaining high standards.
• A proactive approach to work and the ability to work independently when required.
• A good understanding of health and safety practices.
• A full UK driving licence is desirable. PCV licence holders are encouraged to apply.
Why choose Stagecoach?
• Full training provided, including vehicle movements, health and safety, equipment use, and cleaning procedures.
• Competitive rates of pay with opportunities for overtime.
• Generous pension scheme and holiday entitlement.
• Free Stagecoach travel for you and a companion.
• Access to a wide range of retail, leisure, and lifestyle discounts.
• Excellent career development opportunities across engineering, operations, and management.
• A supportive and inclusive workplace where your wellbeing matters.
Our Working Environment
Stagecoach is proud to be an inclusive employer where everyone is treated with dignity and respect. We are committed to creating a workplace where colleagues feel valued, supported, and able to thrive. You'll also have access to wellbeing resources, colleague networks, and a 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme for you and your family.
Ready to join our team?
If you're looking for a varied, active role where you can make a real contribution to keeping Peterborough moving, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply today and start your Stagecoach journey. We look forward to welcoming you on board.
Stagecoach is proudly an inclusive employer, striving for a culture where everyone can be themselves and where all the differences people bring are truly appreciated. We welcome applications from all, irrespective of gender, ethnicity, race, religion, beliefs, disability, neurodiversity, sexual orientation, or age.

Product Mgr II
Do you want to shape the future of customer-focused products?
Can you turn customer insight into product innovation?

Our team owns Identity, Access and API Management for Elsevier. We're focused on making access to our products frictionless and secure — driving innovation and modern access solutions that make customer onboarding easier and authentication seamless, without compromising security. We work collaboratively across Product, Technology, Design, Data, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success to solve real customer access challenges. We value curiosity, innovation, and continuous improvement, and are committed to delivering exceptional experiences for our customers.
About the Role
As a Product Manager II on our team, you will work toward owning the end-to-end value and outcomes of product features — from discovery through to delivery. You will act as the voice of the customer, using market insight, customer feedback, and data to identify opportunities and define solutions that make product access and onboarding seamless — while meeting Elsevier's security and compliance bar.
Working closely with cross-functional teams, you will drive product requirements through specs for your feature area (using genAI and Spec-Driven Development (SDD) as part of your process), execute against the roadmap, and keep your features running well day to day. This role is ideal for a product professional who enjoys combining customer insight, a user-centric approach and applying data-driven decision-making to deliver solutions.
You'll build toward that end-to-end ownership starting with a hands-on placement on our API Management product. You'll partner directly with one or two engineering squads, running discovery through to delivery for your slice of the product, within an overall roadmap and prioritisation set by our senior Product Manager. From there, you'll grow into progressively larger scope, working toward owning the full arc of discovery, delivery, and outcomes for your own product area.
Responsibilities
• Own discovery and requirements for several product areas through the product lifecycle — including cross-product functionality (collaborating with other teams within the wider Identity and Access group) and end-to-end release process including collaboration with go-to-market.
• Own a sub-set of product functionality throughout its entire lifecycle, from discovery to successful release and ongoing performance monitoring. This often includes cross-product functionality, requiring successful collaboration and alignment with other product teams within the Identity and Access space.
• Directly support 1-2 engineering squads by answering engineering queries, using user-research insights and customer feedback to drive new product functionality and collaborating with user experience to ensure the functionality delivered delights users.
• Gather customer insights and translate them into product requirements and solutions.
• Use data, customer feedback, and market analysis to drive product decisions.
• Own ongoing product functionality go-to-market and support, including stakeholder communications for your product area
• Own how success metrics are defined and calculated, ensuring they reflect business outcomes.
• Collaborate with UX, analytics and other teams to deliver high-quality product enhancements.
• Effectively prioritise customer issues, defects, and feature requests for resolution against ongoing product roadmap..
Requirements
• Proven Product Management experience, typically with 4-6 years in a product-focused role.
• Experience owning products, features, or significant areas of product functionality. Experience with API driven products is a plus.
• Strong customer focus with the ability to identify and solve customer problems.
• Demonstrated success delivering product improvements with measurable business impact.
• Excellent analytical and data-driven decision-making skills.
• Strong stakeholder management, communication, and presentation abilities.
• Experience working within Agile software development environments.
• Commercial awareness and understanding of product strategy and business objectives.
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required; a technical or business-related degree is preferred.
If you are interested in the role, please apply with a cover letter and CV.
Work in a way that works for you
We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organisation. With an average length of service of 9 years, we are confident that we offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous wellbeing initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals.
• Working in a hybrid way from both the office and at home
• Working flexible hours - flexing the times you work in the day
Working with us
We are an equal opportunity employer with a commitment to help you succeed. Here, you will find an inclusive, agile, collaborative, innovative and fun environment, where everyone has a part to play. Regardless of the team you join, we promote a diverse environment with co-workers who are passionate about what they do, and how they do it.
Working for you

• Wellbeing programs

1 year:

Investigator, Pensions – Coventry
Make a positive difference to financial services
Contract: Permanent
Working hours: full time (35 hours pw) and part time (28 hours pw)
Salary: £32,577 pa (full time), £26,061.60 pa (part time)
Reporting to: Ombudsman Manager
Start date: 11th January 2027
Our current hybrid policy requires four days per fortnight in the Coventry office.
Join the ‘Becoming an Investigator’ recruitment network and be one of the first to hear about upcoming opportunities in your area: here
As part of your induction, you’ll need to spend your first week in our London office. We will cover your expenses for your time in London.
About us
The Financial Ombudsman Service is an independent, not-for-profit organisation that plays a vital role in UK financial services. Every day we help resolve disputes between consumers, or small businesses, and their financial service providers.
The complaints we deal with vary. In this role, you’ll focus on pensions, where complaints can involve detailed financial information, complex calculations and decisions with a significant impact on a customer’s future.
If we believe a customer hasn’t been treated fairly, we’ll ask the business to put things right. If we think the business isn’t at fault, we’ll explain why. The decisions we make have a huge impact: they can be life-changing for individuals, and they provide insights which are useful for financial businesses.
By joining us as an Investigator, you’ll get to the heart of complaints about pensions. You’ll analyse detailed and sometimes conflicting information, identify what’s missing, ask probing questions and reach fair, evidence-based conclusions. Previous pensions experience is an advantage, but it's not a requirement. We'll give you the technical training you need. What matters is that you're curious, comfortable  working through complexity and able to explain your thinking clearly.
Key responsibilities
As an Investigator new to the role, your journey will start in our Academy, developing the technical knowledge and investigative skills needed to make fair and reasonable decisions. After that, you’ll work as part of a team, supported by an Ombudsman Manager / Operational People Manager, managing your own caseload and prioritising your work.
You’ll be responsible for:
• Investigating complaints about pensions
• Examining detailed evidence, identifying gaps or inconsistencies and asking the right questions to get to the heart of each complaint
• Analysing the information provided, and considering how the relevant rules and regulations apply in the circumstances, reaching a fair and reasonable decision on each case
• Managing your caseload effectively to achieve productivity, quality and timeliness targets
• Managing relationships with consumers, financial businesses and professional representatives, including responding confidently and constructively when your thinking is challenged
• Communicating with empathy and confidence, listening carefully to both sides, asking probing questions and using sound judgement, and
• Communicating your findings clearly, explaining what you think and why through a clear and structured written response
Person specification
You’ll be a self-starter who can prioritise tasks and work well independently. You’ll enjoy digging into detailed information, following evidence, identifying what doesn’t add up and working through problems where the answer may not be immediately obvious. You’ll also have the confidence and people skills to explain and stand behind your decisions.
Your experience could come from financial services, legal or paralegal work, casework, complaints, claims, regulation, compliance, customer services or another role where you have analysed information and reached reasoned conclusions. Previous pensions experience is welcome but not essential, as full training is provided.
Essential Criteria
• Strong analytical skills, with the ability to assess information, identify key issues and reach evidence-based conclusions
• Experience making fair and balanced decisions, explaining your reasoning clearly
• Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex information clearly in both written and verbal formats
• Experience supporting customers through challenging or sensitive situations
• Experience working towards targets, objectives, or service standards
• An interest in developing knowledge of pensions and retirement products
Desirable Criteria
• Experience investigating complex issues, gathering information and identifying key facts to reach a conclusion
• Experience in casework, complaint-handling, legal, regulatory, compliance…

The TP ICAP Group is a world leading provider of market infrastructure.
Our purpose is to provide clients with access to global financial and commodities markets, improving price discovery, liquidity, and distribution of data, through responsible and innovative solutions. Through our people and technology, we connect clients to superior liquidity and data solutions.
The Group is home to a stable of premium brands. Collectively, TP ICAP is the largest interdealer broker in the world by revenue, the number one Energy & Commodities broker in the world, the world’s leading provider of OTC data, and an award winning all-to-all trading platform.
Founded in London in 1866, the Group operates from more than 60 offices in 27 countries.  We are 5,200 people strong.  We work as one to achieve our vision of being the world’s most trusted, innovative, liquidity and data solutions specialist.
Role Overview
The System Architect is responsible for defining and delivering the shared technical and architectural vision for the Agile Release Train (ART). As TP ICAP is a global organization, there will be a requirement to work with geographically distributed teams, and support global deployments as part of the overall architecture.
The technology includes systems (applications, processes and information), shared infrastructure services, shared application services, and their effective integration and reuse across TP ICAP. The System Architect is working to align Feature teams to the Architecture roadmap, and ensure the systems under development support the evolving business need and enables fast reliable implementation of value.
As a core role steering the wider team alongside the Release Train Engineer (RTE) & Product Managers, the System Architect collaborates with the Feature teams to design and develop the architecture and create the Architecture Runway in line with Enterprise standards, patterns and roadmaps.
The role will involve technical leadership with the expectation that the successful candidate will assist in developing skills within teams, and nurturing existing talent. This will include providing expertise on engineering and architecture best practices relating to platforms and user interface delivery.
Key Responsibilities
•
Define and communicate the architecture vision, translating it into Epics, Features, and Stories.
•
Ensure solutions align with business priorities, enterprise architecture, and evolving business needs.
•
Support DevOps practices and the continuous delivery pipeline; contribute to release governance.
•
Promote built-in quality, defining and managing non-functional requirements (NFRs).
•
Collaborate with teams to evolve design, validate implementation, and drive sustainable practices.

Neuberger was founded in 1939 to do one thing: deliver compelling investment results for our clients over the long term. At Cancer Research UK, we exist to beat cancer.
Cancer Research Horizons are looking for a Translation Executive to partner with researchers funded by Cancer Research UK to identify and develop research discoveries that can be translated into innovations that will impact the lives of cancer patients. We are looking for a candidate with excellent scientific judgement, aligned with good understanding of technology scouting within an oncology, medical or pharma environment, IP protection and management, as well as technology validation and progression towards the clinic. You will work closely with CRUK-funded researchers and associated technology transfer offices Cambridge Enterprise, meaning that excellent interpersonal, relationship and stakeholder management skills are crucial.
Cancer Research Horizons (CRH) is the innovation engine of Cancer Research UK (CRUK), translating cutting-edge innovations into effective treatments and diagnostics for cancer patients. With exclusive rights to CRUK’s annual investment of over £300 million in world-class cancer research, we’re a powerful partner in the fight to conquer cancer. We’re currently the second largest oncology out-licensor globally, and to date we’ve played an instrumental role in forming over 60 startup companies with $2.8 billion raised, and bringing 11 new cancer drugs to market, with 6 million doses administered to cancer patients all over the world.
As a Research Translation Executive, you will be responsible for the development and implementation of plans for translation of CRUK funded research at specified key CRUK-funded sites across your region, this role will be focused on the Cambridge region. This will include working with oncology researchers to proactively identify projects and technologies with patient benefit potential, including setting the intellectual property strategy and driving project development by working with a wide variety of internal and external stakeholders.
You will have the opportunity to interact with researchers working on a wide range of scientific and technological areas, including drug discovery/development, biomarkers, diagnostics, medical devices, digital health, and research reagents.
What will you be doing?
• Working with Cambridge Regional Translation Executive to develop S&E strategic initiatives.
• Responsibility for delivery of regional strategic objectives including a Cambridge Cancer Centre or University(s) to support the attainment of overall S&E targets.
• Play an active role as member of R&I regional groupings (CP, Research funding Manager, Institutes & Centres team, Engagement Manager, RBC etc.)

• Play an active role in the management and development of regional translational project portfolio.
• Build and maintain strong, integrated relationships with senior management figures and CRUK-funded scientists at your specified major Centre/Institute/University(s)
• Develop a deep understanding of the research landscape at allocated CRUK site(s) and identify increased collaborative and translational funding opportunities to accelerate progress
• With minimal line management input required, provide appropriate technology transfer services and manage intellectual property protection for portfolio projects in a timely manner.
• Work collaboratively with colleagues from other S&E regions to proactively seek collaborative and synergistic interactions.
• Work in collaboration with internal colleagues focused in other CP core function teams to deliver on CP’s overall operations, performance and strategies;
• Contribute to developing and implementing strategy to enhance and grow the entrepreneurial culture across CRUK-funded researchers, to maximise output of CRUK funding
• Support CP, (including CancerTools) and R&I management with cross department activities as required
• Provide expert translational advice to scientists, major centres and institutions through well-developed communication links
• With minimal line management input required, undertake routine contract negotiation and management for allocated sites in liaison with BD&T and Legal colleagues as required e.g. research collaboration agreements.
What are you looking for?
As job titles vary across organisations, you may currently be working as Senior Translation Manager, Senior Commercialisation Manager or Senior Technology Transfer Manager. Whatever your current job title, you will need to have:
• PhD (or equivalent) in a scientific discipline, ideally in oncology, life sciences, pharma, medicine, or related.
• In-depth experience in translating discovery research and pre-clinical science gained in sectors such as medical technologies, diagnostics, healthcare technologies and pharmaceuticals.  This experience may have been gained in academic technology transfer, industry, healthcare, academia or in non-profit organisations.
• In-depth Knowledge and awareness of oncology drug/technology discovery, IP protection and development and associated science
• Ideally, good working knowledge and experience of the patent filing and prosecution process.

Purpose
PerkinElmer is seeking a Software Product Manager to own the software product roadmap for analytical instrument software aligned to an assigned product line.
Software is an increasingly critical competitive dimension in analytical instrumentation: instrument control software, data processing algorithms, connectivity, and reporting tools increasingly determine customer satisfaction, switching costs, and long-term loyalty. This role ensures that the product line's software strategy is as deliberate and commercially rigorous as its hardware strategy.
The Software Product Manager works at the intersection of product management and software engineering — translating commercial and customer requirements into well-defined software product specifications, prioritising the software backlog against commercial impact, and partnering with the R&D software team to ensure delivery meets market expectations. They are accountable for the software product, not the software development — they set what gets built and why, not how.
We are offering a hybrid working contract split between home and our offices in High Wycombe
Responsibilities
Software Product Strategy & Roadmap
• Own the software product roadmap for the assigned product line — defining the vision, prioritising features and releases, and sequencing development work against commercial opportunity and customer value
• Develop software product requirements: user stories, functional specifications, and acceptance criteria that R&D can act on — with clear priority rationale for each item
• Make evidence-based trade-off decisions about software feature scope, release timing, and technical debt — balancing commercial urgency with software quality and architectural sustainability
• Own the software product versioning and release strategy — coordinating release cadence with hardware product launches and sustaining release cycles
Customer & Market Requirements
• Conduct structured VOC for software: customer interviews, usability feedback sessions, and competitive software benchmarking — generating a minimum of 15 documented customer conversations per year specifically focused on software needs

• Partner with Strategic Segment Managers to understand how regulatory requirements (21 CFR Part 11, GAAMP, OECD GLP) affect software product needs in priority end markets
• Translate hardware NPI requirements into software specification — ensuring instrument control software is developed in parallel with the hardware programme and available at launch
R&D Partnership & Delivery
• Serve as the primary product management interface to the software R&D team — attending sprint reviews, backlog grooming sessions, and software programme milestones
• Maintain a clearly prioritised software backlog — updated regularly, visible to stakeholders, and reflective of current commercial priorities
• Own software release acceptance: define and execute user acceptance testing criteria, certify that software releases meet the defined product requirements before commercial release
• Coordinate beta customer programmes for major software releases — managing site selection, structured feedback collection, and issue resolution before general availability
Commercial Enablement
• Develop software-specific commercial enablement materials: feature release notes, upgrade guides, competitive software comparison sheets, and software-focused demo guides for the sales organisation
• Train the commercial team on major software releases — ensuring field teams can demonstrate, position, and sell software capabilities as a competitive differentiator
• Support the MarComm team with technically accurate software content for campaigns, product brochures, and digital channels

hyperiongrp.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/broadb.description_excerpt:
Who are we?
Howden is a global insurance group with employee ownership at its heart. Together, we have pushed the boundaries of insurance. We are united by a shared passion and no-limits mindset, and our strength lies in our ability to collaborate as a powerful international team comprised of 24,000 employees spanning over 56 countries.
People join Howden for many different reasons, but they stay for the same one: our culture. It’s what sets us apart, and the reason our employees have been turning down headhunters for years. Whatever your priorities – work / life balance, career progression, sustainability, volunteering – you’ll find like-minded people driving change at Howden.
About the role
We build the Android and iOS apps that turn an ordinary phone into a motion sensor for insurance telematics. When a driver gets into their car, the app detects it, records the journey in the background, and uploads it for scoring - with no interaction from the user at all.
This is an Android-first role - where you’d spend most of your time - but you’d join the small team that owns both apps end to end: recording engine, trip lifecycle, upload pipeline, and the app the customer actually sees.
What you’d be working on
· Background journey recording. Foreground services, Activity Recognition and geofencing, surviving Doze, App Standby and aggressive OEM power management. The same battle plays out on iOS - CoreLocation region monitoring, significant location change, background modes.
· BLE beacon detection of a device in the customer’s own vehicle.
· Sensor capture and trip assembly. GPS, accelerometer and gyroscope streams written to disk, compiled into a journey, packaged and uploaded reliably.
· Permission integrity. Ensuring required permissions are always granted and the user notified ASAP if not.
· The customer-facing app: dashboard, journey history and maps, mileage, discounts, onboarding and login - Jetpack Compose on Android, SwiftUI/UIKit on iOS.
· Release engineering: white-label builds for more than one brand, and staged rollouts.
What we’re looking for
Essential
· Strong commercial Android experience in Kotlin, with Coroutines and Flow. You’d also help maintain the iOS app, so you’ll need the appetite to work in Swift.
· Real experience of background execution and its failure modes - foreground services, WorkManager, AlarmManager, broadcast receivers, and why they silently stop firing.
· Comfort with the Android runtime permission model, particularly background location.
· Modern Android UI and architecture: Jetpack Compose, structured concurrency with Coroutines and Flow, DI, local persistence, an HTTP client.
· The instinct to write tests for concurrency, not just happy paths. Most of what breaks here is a race, a lifecycle edge, or a restart mid-flight.
· Practical fluency with AI coding agents, and a clear-eyed view of what they’re bad at. We use them regularly, and we want someone who prompts deliberately, knows when to stop and do it by hand, and reviews the output critically.
· Willingness to debug from evidence - device logs, CSV traces, ANR and crash reports - and add relevant and targeted logging to catch a future problem.
Desirable
· Existing iOS experience - Swift, SwiftUI/UIKit, and the CoreLocation-driven background model. You’d pick this up on the job regardless, but knowing it already is a real plus.
· Prior work in telematics, IoT, fitness/activity tracking, or navigation - anything that runs unattended and drains a battery is the closest analogue to what we do.
· BLE and the ways both Bluetooth stacks disappoint you.
· Location and sensor fusion, GPS accuracy, filtering noisy signals.
· Firebase - Crashlytics, Analytics and Remote Config - and using production telemetry to chase down the bugs you can’t reproduce on your own desk.
You don’t need an insurance background.
How we work
Small team, direct ownership. You’d take tickets end to end - investigate, fix, write it up, raise the PR, ensure QA knows what to test, then monitor the release. Be aware that these are long-lived apps: the recording engine has been evolving since 2017, and there are areas of it that nobody fully understands any more.
Occasionally there’s careful archaeology in code you can’t take on trust, and we’d expect you to leave it better documented than you found it.
Testing happens heavily on physical devices, because a simulator cannot tell you what a phone does in a car - in practice that means recording real test journeys on company phones and test accounts, so regular access to a vehicle, as driver or passenger, is useful. We’ll provide a Mac and phones to test with.
What do we offer in return?

•
Support implementation of reliability-centred maintenance practices.

Strong mechanical fault-finding and problem-solving ability.
•
Ability to read technical drawings, P&IDs, and OEM documentation.
•
Skilled in maintaining rotating machinery (pumps, blowers, mixers, compressors).

Experience with mechanical seals, bearings, alignment, and coupling systems.

Knowledge of water/wastewater treatment processes (preferred).

Good communication and teamwork, working alongside operators, engineers, and contractors.

Ability to prioritise work, especially during breakdowns.

Strong safety awareness and compliance-led mindset.

Recognised mechanical engineering qualification (NVQ Level 3 / City & Guilds / apprenticeship or equivalent).

Proven experience as a Mechanical Fitter or Maintenance Technician.

Experience in an industrial, utilities, or process-plant environment.

Confined space training (NC1/NC2).

Experience within the water or wastewater industry specifically.

Water hygiene card (EUSR).

IOSH Working Safely or similar safety qualification.

Welding or fabrication skills.

Based at treatment works, pumping stations, or regional sites.

Outdoor work in varying weather conditions.

• Direct experience with crypto assets and/or fiat-backed stablecoins, including fair value measurement, classification, and disclosure.

• Experience with digital assets, fintech, payments, treasury, settlement,…

Plan headroom for growth so capacity, licensing and footprint decisions do not become tomorrow’s constraint.
•
Maintain a single published view of obsolescence and technical debt, with the cost of inaction quantified.

Kent & East Sussex | Salary up to £32,000 | £1,000 Joining Bonus
A nursing role where your skills make a difference
If you're an RVN who enjoys hands-on nursing, values good clinical standards and wants to be part of a team where nurses play an important role in patient care, we'd love to introduce you to Cinque Ports Vets.
We're an established, RCVS-accredited practice with four sites across Kent and East Sussex, offering a varied caseload, excellent clinical facilities and an experienced nursing team.
Our nurses are actively involved in patient care, nurse consultations, vaccinations and supporting surgical and medical cases. We want you to feel confident using your skills, sharing your knowledge and continuing to develop as a veterinary professional.
What makes nursing at Cinque Ports different?
Our branches are much more than satellite consulting clinics. Each has its own specialisms, alongside the facilities to investigate cases and carry out surgical procedures.
At the heart of our practice is Kingsnorth, our RCVS-accredited Veterinary Hospital, which holds Gold ISFM Cat Friendly Accreditation. The hospital provides 24-hour emergency care, 365 days a year, with Vets Now onsite supporting continuity of care for patients.
Across our four sites, our facilities include digital radiography, dental X-ray, ultrasound, Doppler ultrasonography, ECG, in-house laboratories, endoscopy, video endoscopy and bronchoscopy.
For an RVN, this means working in a clinical environment with the equipment, colleagues and opportunities to make good use of your nursing knowledge.
Your role within the nursing team
You'll work closely with our veterinary surgeons, fellow RVNs and nursing leadership team to deliver high standards of patient care and a positive client experience.
Your role will include:
• Providing high-quality nursing care across medical, surgical and hospital patients.
• Using your nursing skills to support clinical procedures, patient monitoring and recovery.
• Supporting nurse consultations, client education and communication.
• Maintaining accurate clinical records and excellent infection control standards.
• Contributing to clinical audits, quality improvement and patient care initiatives.
• Sharing knowledge, supporting colleagues and participating in ongoing professional development.
We're looking for someone who takes pride in their nursing, communicates well with clients and colleagues, and enjoys being part of a supportive, collaborative clinical team.
A place to keep developing
We recognise the value that skilled veterinary nurses bring to clinical practice.
You'll be working alongside experienced RVNs who undertake nurse consultations and vaccinations, with opportunities to learn from colleagues and contribute your own ideas.
Professional development is encouraged through funded external CPD, in-house learning and access to the extensive Linnaeus online CPD programme. As part of Linnaeus, you'll also have access to wider career progression opportunities.
Working hours
The role averages 40.78 hours per week over a 9-week rota cycle, with a standard working pattern of 40 hours across five weekdays.
You'll participate in a 2-in-9 weekend rota. One weekend shift is included in your contracted hours, while the second provides a day in lieu in line with practice policy.
What you'll receive
Alongside a competitive salary and joining bonus, our benefits include:
• 5 weeks' annual leave plus bank holidays and birthday leave

Gather customer intelligence and feedback to support proactive participation in product enhancement and new product development.
•
Ensure accurate management of CRM records (SFDC) within the territory
•
Ensure that product knowledge and customer communication are maintained to the highest standard.
•
Provide product samples and quotations to customers in a timely manner.
What You'll Bring
•
Degree or equivalent experience in a life sciences discipline, such as molecular biology, microbiology, biological sciences, biochemistry, medical science or a related field.
•
Proven field sales experience – 2 years minimum – within the UK life sciences market, ideally with laboratory consumables, instrumentation and/or sample management solutions.
•
Ability to demonstrate technical products and clearly explain sample management workflows, customer value and application benefits.
•
Commercially focused and target-driven, with strong territory planning, pipeline management, account development and customer relationship skills.
•
Good awareness of the UK laboratory and life sciences marketplace, including customer needs, market trends and competitor activity.
•
Self-motivated, organised and confident working independently across a defined territory while contributing effectively as part of a wider sales team.
•
Full UK driving licence and willingness to travel regularly across Oxford, Wales and the South West UK.
Our Offer
•
Become part of a company that makes a positive contribution to launching groundbreaking scientific developments and therapies.
•
Contribute to innovative cell therapies and be part of revolutionary cancer therapies.
•
Take advantage of the operational opportunities in a growing, modern and innovative company within the healthcare and life sciences industry.
•
Experience intensive knowledge sharing and close cooperation within a worldwide network of customers, colleagues and partners.

Participate in national and international company events.

Individual development opportunities to strengthen your international competencies and language skills.

Samples are precious. Materials matter. That’s why Azenta exists – we are purpose-built to serve the unique challenges of modern drug discovery, clinical development and commercialisation. With comprehensive solutions spanning sample management, analysis, automation and informatics, you can have complete confidence that your samples are safe and optimised, and your programme has the best chance of success.
Azenta Life Sciences offers a wide range of sample management solutions, with the sample at the core. Consumables and instruments for various life sciences industries, including biobanking, compound management, consumer genomics, synthetic biology and basic research. Our products, such as 2D-coded sample storage tubes, readers and sample management systems, support diverse customer applications, from basic research to molecular diagnostics.
We prioritise sample integrity throughout the entire lifecycle, from sample collection and preparation through PCR analysis to cryopreservation and storage. Our temperature management systems, including workstations, modules, dishes, cryo boxes and other essential consumables, meet the diverse needs of the life sciences sector.

Kobre & Kim is a global law firm focused exclusively on disputes and investigations, with a strength in complex cross-border matters. The firm’s work spans financial products and services litigation, insolvency disputes, intellectual property litigation, international judgment enforcement and asset recovery, and U.S. government enforcement and regulatory investigations.
Kobre & Kim has achieved significant results for clients in high-stakes, cross-border matters. Recent successes include winning a US $604.9 million jury verdict and a total award exceeding US $833 million for a green fuel company in a landmark U.S. trial as well as securing the dismissal in the English courts of the Kingdom of Spain’s challenge to recognition of a €120 million ICSID award.
The Analyst Experience
Analysts receive a competitive compensation and benefits package, along with opportunities for professional development, mentorship, and meaningful exposure to the firm’s work, including:
• £54,000 per annum, based on a full-time work schedule, plus eligibility for a significant discretionary annual bonus.
• Weekly hybrid office model with three days in the office and flexibility to work remotely for the remaining two days.
• Two weeks of study leave and an exam preparation stipend for relevant examinations.
• Flexibility to use unused study leave or personal time off for external vacation schemes.
• A lawyer mentor and stipend to support mentorship activities.
• Regular team events and activities.
• Language learning stipend.
• Opportunities to travel subject to case needs.
• Additional benefits disclosed at the offer stage.
Your Impact
Our Analysts are an elite cohort of early-career individuals who gain substantive, hands-on experience supporting complex international civil and criminal financial litigation. As members of case teams, Analysts work alongside lawyers and business professionals, with exposure to client matters, pro bono work, knowledge management and global business development. The work is varied and fast-paced, with responsibilities adapting to the needs of each matter.
We are seeking intellectually curious graduates with strong research, writing, analytical and problem-solving skills. An interest in law, disputes, investigations or financial markets is a plus, but a legal background is not required.

These skills open doors across a wide range of careers and industries. • Ability to work outside standard business hours as needed, including late nights, weekends, and holidays, depending on assignments.
• Excellent teamwork, organization, project management, and attention to detail, with creative and anticipatory thinking skills.
• Strong work ethic, proactivity, and ability to perform under pressure in a fast-paced environment.

Full Time | £47,655.00 - £55,598.00 + London Weighting (£3,500)

Ordnance Survey is one of the Britain’s most impactful technology and data companies.  We’re part of everyday life, with our data being used up to 40 times by the average person. We operate an invisible layer that enables the digital world to understand the physical world.
Geovation exists to expand this impact further, we want to push the boundaries of what is possible with location data.  We’re passionate about bringing entrepreneurs, innovators and geospatial experts together to solve real world problems in new ways.
Our Farringdon hub is a vibrant space where first-time founders collaborate with experienced entrepreneurs and geospatial specialists. It’s a place where ideas become reality. We host events, encourage creativity, and help build the next generation of data-driven applications.
Our incubation team builds and experiments directly with start-ups, helping them turn their ideas into products and building viable businesses around them.
About the Role:
As the Incubator Manager at Geovation you’re responsible for making sure the startups we take into our programme can use it as a launch pad for their ambitions. You’ll play a leading role in finding and selecting which startups we support, and it will be up to you to develop bespoke support programmes that enable them to build sustainable businesses around the products that the technical part of the team helps to build.
You will work closely with the Incubator Lead and our technical and ecosystem teams along with third parties and OS experts to deliver this support.  You’ll also have a role in the wider community – as one of the key people in the team who really ‘gets founders’ and know what they need. You will build strong relationships with founders and understand the challenges facing their business, but you will also be responsible for making sure the detail behind the programme works.
We’re looking for someone who thrives on building relationships, influencing others and making things happen. You’ll take the lead on some of our key strategic partnerships, building strong relationships across Geovation, Ordnance Survey and our external network.
You’ll need to be confident working with senior stakeholders, balancing different priorities and bringing people together around shared goals. Leadership experience would be an advantage, particularly as you’ll help shape direction and support others to succeed.
In this role, you will:
• Scout for startups to invite to apply to the programme in response to target areas set by the Team Leads, manage the recruitment and selection process and facilitate the administrative sides of the process, including appropriate due diligence and finance.
• Be the main point of contact for startups within the programme. Work with the Incubator Lead to design support on a startup-by-startup basis to ensure support aligns with the wider strategy of the team.
• Lead on the design and delivery of non-technical support jointly with the Ecosystem team, utilising programme alumni, Geovation, OS employees and third parties.
• Be an advocate for the power of location data, the impact that startups have on creating new markets and industries for OS data and advocate for the specific startups we support.
• Look for connections between different founder needs, OS capabilities, market opportunities and activity happening across the wider Geovation ecosystem.
• Be a key part of making the Geovation Hub is a vibrant creative place to work and a safe, inclusive, welcoming, and well-maintained space for members and visitors.  This includes involvement in events and activation as well as some formal Fire, health & safety responsibilities for the Geovation Hub and ad-hoc tasks required as part of a small team running a busy coworking space.

About you and how we work
We’re looking for someone who is passionate about startups and knows what they need, ideally you will have worked in or with start-ups in the past and can bring that experience to bear.
We want someone who’s comfortable tailoring the message for the diverse audiences we work with, helping communicate the value of our community that we’ve created over the last 15 years.
You’ll need to demonstrate:
• Experience of creating bespoke development programmes based on an understanding of needs, sometimes developing and delivering workshops themselves.
• Outstanding interpersonal, relationship building, coaching and mentoring skills and the ability to deploy them in with first time founders and serial entrepreneurs even when things aren’t going well
• The ability to make sense of complex or ambiguous situations, connect different pieces of information and turn those insights into clear priorities, actions and opportunities.
• Experience of scouting for leading edge startups based on specific briefs – and building relationships with those startups to understand and ‘sell’ their fit with Geovation.
• An experimental and continuous improvement mindset, willing to try things out with the aim of learning and proving / disproving a hypothesis.
• The desire and ability to be part of a flexible, small team that collaborates to achieve joint goals, regardless of the exact work to be done.
Particularly useful experience
Any of the following would be beneficial but are not essential:
• Experience working with startups, whether through an accelerator, incubator, venture builder, startup programme or within a startup itself.
• Experience supporting early-stage founders through coaching, mentoring, advisory work, scouting or selection.
• Experience coordinating partnerships, programmes or activity across multiple organisations or stakeholders.
• Experience improving operational processes, systems or ways of working.
The Rewards
We want you to love what you do and feel supported to do your best work.

Job Description:
Paid Social Manager (B2B) | Permanent | London | Hybrid Working
Dentsu is an integrated growth and transformation partner to the world’s leading organizations. Founded in 1901 in Tokyo, Japan, and now present in over 145 countries and regions, it has a proven track record of nurturing and developing innovations, combining the talents of its global network of leadership brands to develop impactful and integrated growth solutions for clients. Dentsu delivers end-to-end experience transformation (EX) by integrating its services across Media, CXM and Creative, while its business transformation (BX) mindset pushes the boundaries of transformation and sustainable growth for brands, people and society.
We’re hiring a Paid Social Manager as part of our London B2B team. The purpose of this role is to lead and manage the planning, execution and optimisation of B2B paid social campaigns, ensuring best in class delivery, strategic excellence and strong day today client communication.
You will help clients reach and influence professional audiences, generate high quality demand and drive measurable commercial outcomes across the B2B funnel.
Purpose of the Role
The Paid Social Manager will play a key role in leading the strategy and delivery of B2B paid social activity across multiple platforms.
You will be responsible for crafting audience first media approaches, optimising full funnel performance and ensuring campaigns deliver against their goals & objectives.
This role requires someone with proven B2B experience, a strong grasp of how paid social supports long and complex buyer journeys and the ability to translate data into actionable insights that drive meaningful impact.
Key Responsibilities
•
Developing B2B-specific paid social strategies aligned to client business goals, target industries, buying committees and the full customer journey.
•
Partnering closely with clients to define KPIs such as marketing-qualified leads (MQLs) and sales-qualified leads (SQLs).
•
Leading the end-to-end activation of paid social campaigns across platforms such as LinkedIn, Meta, Reddit, X and emerging B2B environments.
•
Managing always on activity alongside campaign bursts, ensuring the right balance of awareness, consideration and conversion tactics tailored for long sales cycles.
•
Ensuring all campaigns launch on time, meet quality standards and stay within budget.
•
Serving as the day-to-day B2B paid social expert for clients, providing clear recommendations, performance updates and strategic guidance.
•
Building strong relationships with Client Services, Strategy, Data and other Paid Media teams to ensure an integrated & aligned approach.
•
Translating complex performance data into simple, actionable client narratives.
•
Owning optimisation frameworks that aim to improve performance e.g. lead quality, cost-per lead reductions etc.
•
Producing insightful reporting that connects paid social performance to business impacts, using CRM or marketing automation data where applicable.
•
Identifying growth opportunities across accounts, including new platform tests, creative enhancements, audience refinements and measurement evolution.
Qualifications + Skills
•
Strong experience planning and managing B2B paid social campaigns, preferably within an agency or client facing environment.
•
Deep understanding of LinkedIn Campaign Manager.
•
Ability to build strategic audience plans that target job titles, functions, industries etc.
•
Solid grasp of B2B marketing principles, including funnel design, lead qualification, nurture flows and CRM integration.
•
Exceptional analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex performance data and connect it to business outcomes.
•
Confident communicator & presenter.
•
Proven track record of delivering successful B2B performance for clients (e.g., CPL, MQL, SQL, pipeline contribution).
What we offer
•
This is a permanent role
•
The team is based in our London office but operates under flexible working arrangements.
•
As well as a competitive salary, you’ll enjoy a benefits package that you can tailor to your needs.
Inclusion and Diversity
At Dentsu, we embrace diversity and inclusion, valuing the unique perspectives and contributions of every individual. We believe that diversity fuels creativity and innovation, benefiting our employees, partners, and communities.
We welcome applications from all individuals, regardless of race, ethnicity, nationality, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, marital status, or any other protected characteristic. Beyond recruitment, we strive to create an environment where everyone feels respected, supported, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work.
We recognise the importance of work-life balance and are open to discussing flexible working arrangements for all roles. If you need reasonable adjustments due to a disability or medical condition during our recruitment process, please contact us at accommodations@dentsu.com, quoting the reference number of the role that you are applying for. Your needs will be handled with respect and confidentiality to ensure an inclusive and accessible experience.

PIMCO is a global leader in active fixed income with deep expertise across public and private markets. We invest our clients’ capital across a range of fixed income and credit opportunities, leveraging our decades of experience navigating complex debt markets. Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking.  We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. 2027 Summer Internship – Product Analyst, EMEA
Internship positions are located at PIMCO’s London office
You’re eligible to apply if you:
• Are an undergraduate or masters student currently pursuing a degree with an expected graduation date of December 2027 – June 2028
• Are available to begin full time employment at a PIMCO office between January 2028 – August 2028
• Are on track to achieve a minimum 2.1 degree (or equivalent)
• Are business proficient in English
You’ll excel as a Product Analyst if you:
• Have a passion for financial markets, macroeconomics, and investment management
• Possess a strong analytical skill set with a good understanding of programming languages being a plus
• Demonstrate proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint
• Have the ability to relay complex ideas clearly
• Possess excellent verbal and written communication skills
• Desire to join a fast-paced, high performance culture
• Are results oriented, with strong attention to detail and time management skills
• Have demonstrated curiosity and experience in using new emerging technologies and AI tools in your work or school projects to solve problems and drive better outcomes

You will work within the Product Strategy Group, a global team of over 130 professionals responsible for financial market expertise (both internally and externally), strategic business management, entrepreneurship and marketing for a wide range of PIMCO product lines. • You’ll receive feedback at mid- and end-of-summer as part of a formal review process to keep you on the path to meeting your summer goals
• Want to learn more? Hear about The PIMCO Internship Experience from past interns

How you should apply:
Applications open in September 2026. We review applications on a rolling basis and encourage you to apply by submitting your resume as soon as you are ready.

About the Opportunity
Job Type: Permanent
Application Deadline: 30 October 2026
Job Description
Title Technical Specialist - Detection, Engineering and Automation
Department FIL – Global Cybersecurity Operations
Location Kingswood, Surrey
Reports To Senior Manager - Detection, Engineering and Automation
Level 4
We share a commitment to making things better for clients and each other. We continually explore new technology and different ways of working to put our clients first. So bring your boldest ideas to our Cyber Defense Operations team and feel like you’re making progress.
About your team
Technology function across FIL is responsible for all global aspects of Technology, Digital, Cybersecurity, and Innovation. Fidelity is a value-driven, customer-obsessed organization and in Technology we are fortunate to play a direct role in helping our clients with one of the most important aspects of their lives – their financial well-being.
Within the Technology function is our Global Cyber & Information Security (GCIS) that operates enterprise security services and controls. These are designed to mitigate Cyber and Information Security risks ensuring that Fidelity's business operates securely. The Technical Cybersecurity teams monitor both the internal and external threat environment, responding to security alerts and events in close to real time, as well as providing security assurance and access management services across the enterprise technology and business environment. Our global innovative Cyber Defence Operations team sits within GCIS and provides proactive, cutting-edge solutions to protect clients’ digital assets and infrastructure against evolving cyber threats.
The Detection Engineering & Automation team within our Global Cybersecurity Operations focuses on the development of automated detection capabilities to reduce manual effort of the Global Cybersecurity Operations team freeing up time to focus on real cyber threats.  They ensure that security controls are performing effectively and efficiently and that they are feeding into automation technologies allowing the organisation to make intelligent correlated decisions.
About your role
The Detection Engineering & Automation Specialist plays a critical hands‑on role in strengthening the Global Cybersecurity Operations capability by building, maintaining and enhancing the security tooling that underpins our detection and response functions. The ideal candidate will work deeply across technologies including SIEM, SOAR, EDR, email security and cloud security platforms, contributing engineering expertise to ensure these controls operate effectively and deliver high‑quality telemetry.
You will be responsible for developing and improving detections, building CI/CD pipelines, onboarding new log sources, implementing automation and supporting technical investigations during security incidents. The ideal candidate has experience using a wide range of security technologies to enhance detection coverage, streamline analyst workflows and support the ongoing maintenance and optimisation of critical security controls. This role is essential in supporting engineering maturity and ensuring our cyber defence capabilities remain modern, integrated and responsive to evolving threats.
About you
Key Responsibilities
The Detection, Automation and Engineering Specialist will be responsible to:
•
Build, maintain and enhance security detections using Sentinel‑as‑Code, ensuring accurate and high‑quality analytics.
•
Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines to automate deployment of detections, automation playbooks and configuration updates.
•

About Us
Wellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 60 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. As a private partnership, we believe our ownership structure fosters a long-term view that aligns our perspectives with those of our clients.
About the Role
The Position
The “Funds Group” sits within the broader Client Platform, and is responsible for the end to end fund lifecycle spanning the full range of Wellington’s product offerings worldwide, including equity, fixed income, multi-asset and alternatives strategies. Wellington Management sponsors over 300 commingled investment vehicles globally with AUM of over $150 billion. Within Funds Group this role will predominantly focus on the ‘global’ businesses (“WMF Global”), and as of 30 June 2026, WMF Global comprised of just over 70 funds domiciled predominantly in Luxembourg (UCITS and AIFs) and Ireland (UCITS), as well as in Cayman, Singapore and China, with total assets of circa US$50 billion.
This role sits within the Fund Product team, and the role presents an exciting opportunity to be part of a rapidly growing group, which develops and oversees a variety of commingled funds offered to a diverse set of Wellington’s clients from over 50 countries worldwide.
Responsibilities
This role will primarily focus on leading the coordination efforts around the creation, oversight, and maintenance of regulatory documentation for the WMF Global business. The role will work very closely with the EMEA Funds Legal team and other Fund Product team members, as well as investment teams and subject matter experts across the business. This role will be the point-person for creating or maintaining ‘best in class’ legal and regulatory documentation for various fund activities covering our multiple fund structures and domiciles. In addition, the individual may support members of the Fund Product team in the development of funds and related change activity and other ad-hoc strategic or regulatory projects, and this may bridge other fund domiciles.

•
Take a leading role in project managing the end-to-end process for the prospectus cycles for our various fund ranges and domiciles. Lead and evolve this process for efficiencies as we expand into new distribution markets e.g., most recently Asia retail registrations for cross border UCITS funds.
•
Establish consistency and quality across the various fund offering documents, including shareholder notices and help embed a control and oversight process working with multiple stakeholder groups, that includes partnership with legal and external counsel and relevant vendors. Documentation updates (prospectuses, internal governance communications, KIID/KID, regulatory forms, etc) – helping to ensure that all the right documents are generated, consistency of language adopted and delivered on time for the appropriate governance meetings.

Regulator comments – there can be several rounds of comments, from multiple regulators associated with each submission, running concurrently. This effort also needs to convey a sense of urgency to impacted SME’s as well as ensuring accuracy of responses.
•
Client notifications – help draft content and incorporate necessary client communication notice periods into the master scheduling of ‘moving parts’.
•
External vendor management – owning the relationship with external vendors responsible for the registration and publication of the prospectus, shareholder notices and other fund documentation.
•
Implementation updates – coordinate periodic internal communication summarizing upcoming changes and implementation items to the various stakeholder groups impacted by a new fund and fund changes, bringing in the various SMEs where necessary.
Other projects/responsibilities
•
Together with the WMF Fund Product team, provide general fund expertise and act as subject matter expert to internal stakeholders for client-specific queries that cannot be fielded by client or fund service teams, such as specific information on fund documentation changes and shareholder communications.
•
Lead or assist with ad hoc Fund Product projects. These may include:
•
Annual Fee and Prospectus review exercise working with investment teams and industry data to ensure that our fees remain competitive and reasonable and the Prospectus is correctly aligned with how our funds are being managed.
•
Seed capital and share class reviews to ensure that we are being stewards of the firm’s resources.
•
Assist with the management of EMT (European MiFID Template) and EET (European ESG Template) production and dissemination ensuring we provide distributors with the information needed to meet their MiFID II obligations.
•
Aid in commercial and fiduciary reviews of the fund range to ensure that funds are scaling in line with expectations and have a diversified client base.

An individual likely to have spent +3 years working within asset management or related industry.

Preference for individual who has hands on experience with legal or regulatory documents and content creation. Direct experience working in a product/legal role, and a proximity to fund vehicles being highly valued.
•
Individuals with project management experience. Exceptional organisational skills and attention to detail.
•
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to simplify the complex.
•
Willingness to take initiative, demonstrate accountability and ownership but also having good judgement about when to seek the wider audience first.
•
A desire to evolve as an individual contributor to the team and over time expand the role to take on more responsibility for components of the fund lifecycle process.
•
Collaborative and positive mindset, and good inter-personal skills. Must be able to navigate cross-functional projects and establish healthy working relationships.

Grace under pressure, an ethos for hard work, and master prioritiser.

About the Role
As an Analog Design Engineer Intern at Analog Devices (ADI), you will work alongside experienced engineers on the design, simulation, and characterization of high-performance analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits (ICs). You will contribute to the development of circuits such as amplifiers, filters, data converters, and clocking solutions, while gaining hands-on experience with industry-standard design and simulation tools including Cadence and SPICE.
In this role, you will support circuit design, simulation, layout, silicon validation, and laboratory testing activities, developing practical skills across the full IC development lifecycle. This internship offers an excellent opportunity to learn from industry experts and contribute to cutting-edge semiconductor products used in a wide range of applications.
Key Responsibilities
• Assist in the design, simulation, and verification of analog and mixed-signal circuits, including amplifiers, filters, and data converters.
• Use industry-standard simulation tools such as SPICE and Cadence to analyse circuit performance and validate design concepts.
• Support IC layout activities with a focus on performance, matching, reliability, and manufacturability.
• Perform laboratory measurements and characterization using equipment such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and power supplies.
• Collaborate with senior engineers to debug design issues, optimize circuit performance, and support silicon bring-up activities.
• Document design results, test findings, and technical analyses in a clear and structured manner.

• Fundamental understanding of analog circuit design, including amplifiers, filters, biasing circuits, and feedback systems.
• Basic knowledge of mixed-signal IC design principles and the interaction between analog and digital circuitry.
• Familiarity with circuit simulation and modelling using tools such as SPICE or equivalent EDA tools.
• Understanding of CMOS technologies and semiconductor device fundamentals.
• Exposure to integrated circuit layout concepts, including matching, parasitic effects, and layout best practices.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.
• Effective communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.

As a Manager within our Private Capital Corporate Tax team you will have the opportunity to work with a varied client base, from owner-managed business to private equity backed businesses. You will:
• Management the corporation tax compliance cycle for a portfolio of clients
• Be advising a broad range of clients on a range of tax issues, covering a broad range of compliance and advisory projects

• You’ll possess strong knowledge of UK corporate tax legislation and a working knowledge of international concepts
• You’ll have reviewed work and supervised people in a tax environment
• You’ll have gained experience working within a professional services environment
• You’ll have experience of managing a large portfolio of tax clients
• You’ll have demonstrable Business Development experience
• An eagerness to develop deep knowledge of the firm’s services and capabilities
Knowing we’re right for you
The culture at Grant Thornton is what sets us apart, we’re known for our inclusive culture and creating environments where all our people can flourish. The things that set you apart, we value them, and this helps us all to perform at our best.
Our values are the unwavering principles that shape our daily behaviours and decisions, alongside our drive to do the right thing. We’re looking for people who align with our values and are purposefully driven, actively curious and candid but kind. You can learn more about our values in practice here.

And more. Visit our benefits section to read more.
How we work

Our how we work framework gives flexibility in where, how, and when we work to deliver the best results for our clients, whilst helping you keep a balance between work and life. Life is more than work, the things you do, and the people you’re with outside of work matter, that’s why we’re happy to look at flexible working options for all our roles.  That is how it should be. We embrace hybrid working, and typically spend two days a week collaborating in the office or out with clients per week.
We’re looking for people who can help drive the business forward, who want to contribute, spark fresh ideas and go beyond expectations. People who want to be able to proudly do what’s right, for the firm, our clients, our people and themselves. It’s how it should be.

• Language Skills: Fluency in English.

Blanks

Marine, Cargo & Logistics Insurance Apprenticeship Programme 2027

Location: London
Start date: September 2027
Salary: £28,000

Marine, Cargo & Logistics Insurance Apprenticeship Programme
Help Keep Global Trade Moving
Ready to earn, learn and launch your career? This is more than your first job. You’ll gain real experience, work towards a recognised qualification and build skills that will shape your future.
Every day, ships and businesses transport goods around the world. Our Marine, Cargo & Logistics teams help clients protect their ships, cargo and transport operations if something goes wrong, such as damage, theft, accidents or delays.
You’ll gain exposure across our different Marine, Cargo and Logistics teams, working alongside our brokers, technicians and claims professionals to learn how we support our clients. This will give you experience in several areas and help you discover where your interests and strengths lie.
You’ll join Howden on a permanent role and complete an 18-month development programme designed to develop your technical knowledge, professional skills and confidence to kick start your career.
What you’ll be doing?
You will begin with a structured induction before joining our Marine, Cargo & Logistics team, where you will work alongside experienced colleagues and gradually take on more responsibility.
During the programme, you'll:
• Rotate across different areas of Marine, Cargo and Logistics insurance.
• Learn how businesses use insurance to protect their ships, cargo and transport operations.
• Support the team with processing insurance information and client requests.
• Learn how an insurance policy moves from a client’s first enquiry through to placement, servicing and renewal.
• Support the team with keeping our systems and client records up to date.
Who are we looking for?
No insurance experience is needed; we’ll teach you everything you need to know!
You'll be:
• Curious and interested in learning about insurance, shipping and global trade.
• Comfortable asking questions and sharing your ideas.
• Organised and able to manage different tasks.
• A clear and confident communicator.
• Comfortable working with numbers and information.
• Collaborative and enjoy working with different people.
• Motivated to learn, solve problems and develop your career.
• Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment.
To be eligible for our apprenticeship, you must:
• Have the full and unrestricted right to work in the UK.
• Have lived permanently in the UK for the last 3 years.
• Have achieved a grade C/4 in GCSE English and Maths.
• Not already hold a qualification that significantly overlaps with the content of this apprenticeship.
Application process
Our application process is designed to help you show your potential, not to test what you already know!
• Online application form – no CV required: We believe you're more than just a document, so we won’t ask you to submit a CV. Please upload a blank document on the application form.
• Online gamified assessment: We’ve created games that will help us understand your natural strengths and how you approach different situations. There are no right or wrong answers. You can complete this stage on your phone or laptop, whichever suits you best!
• Pre-recorded video interview: You will record your answers to a few questions using your phone or laptop, giving you the chance to tell us more about yourself in your own time in a relaxed setting.
• Assessment centre: Our final stage is an in-person assessment centre at one of our offices. You'll take part in some fun group activities and meet our team in a relaxed setting. This day is all about getting to know you better and for you to see what it's like to be part of Howden and experience our culture. We'll cover all your travel costs for this day, because where you are now, shouldn’t hold back your future!
Why should you apply?
At Howden, people are at the heart of everything we do. As an employee-owned business, we believe success is built through collaboration, learning and supporting one another. You'll gain exposure to an exciting global industry, receive structured development throughout the summer and build relationships that could shape your future career.
You'll also benefit from:

The Role
Focussing on our Sportsbook product, we’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build and evolve our next-generation trading risk platform, powering real-time liability and exposure management across multiple brands and markets.
You’ll primarily work on our Core Liability engine — a modular, event-driven system  — delivering fast, accurate, and real-time insight into live positions and risk. This platform underpins critical trading decisions and represents a major step forward in scalability, resilience, and streaming architecture across our technology estate.
What You’ll Do
•
Design and build distributed, real-time streaming components within a Flink-based architecture.
•
Develop and maintain services that process the full bet lifecycle, from acceptance through settlement, cancellation, and cashout.
•
Implement complex financial calculations, including multi-bet and bet-builder logic, ensuring accuracy and consistency at scale.
•
Build systems that aggregate exposure and generate real-time risk insights across outcomes, markets, and customers.
•
Contribute to a granular alerting framework that detects and publishes meaningful changes in liability.
•
Ensure correctness in a high-throughput environment through robust handling of ordering, duplication, and idempotency.
•
Optimise streaming jobs for latency, throughput, and resource efficiency.
•
Collaborate closely with trading and product teams to translate domain requirements into scalable, reliable systems.
•
Contribute to a modular architecture where components evolve independently and scale with increasing demand.
What You’ll Work On
•
A real-time liability platform providing live visibility into exposure and risk across brands and jurisdictions.
•
A Flink-based streaming ecosystem composed of specialised components for ingestion, enrichment, calculation, aggregation, and alerting.
•
Event-driven systems that process high volumes of bet events with strong consistency guarantees.
•
Outcome-level alerting that enable faster and more informed trading decisions.
•
Integration with downstream systems, including trader-facing tools.
Your experience
•
5+ years software engineering experience in building distributed systems.
•
Excellent Java skills
•
Experience with streaming technologies (Apache Flink preferred; Kafka Streams, Spark Streaming, etc.).
•
Solid understanding of event-driven architecture and asynchronous processing patterns.
•
Experience handling data consistency challenges such as at-least-once processing, idempotency, and event ordering.
•
Experience building high-throughput, low-latency systems in production environments.
•
Ability to model complex domain logic and translate business requirements into robust technical solutions.
•
Experience in cloud computing, ideally AWS.
•
Proactive and ability to deal with and account for uncertainty, with the flexibility to learn by iteration.
Nice to Have
•
Experience in sports betting, trading platforms, or financial systems.
•
Experience building real-time alerting or monitoring systems.
•
Exposure to modern data platforms or lakehouse architectures.

What does the job involve?
​The Greater Wash (GRW) unit of the North Sea Region (NOS) has responsibility for the safe and efficient operations of the Dudgeon (402MW), Hywind Scotland (30MW) and Sheringham Shoal (317MW) offshore wind farms.
As part of the NOS strategy to realise value from establishing geographical hubs, Great Yarmouth will serve as the central operations base from which operations and maintenance (O&M) activities for both Dudgeon and Sheringham Shoal will be managed.
The new model will establish a shared logistical concept whereby a Service Operations Vessel (SOV) and Crew Transfer Vessel (CTV) are used to carry out operations. Operations on the assets will be carried out under a common set of safety rules and resources will be given the necessary training to be able to work across both wind farms enabling greater flexibility. Integrating the two assets will set up the GRW for further scale and value creation and growth opportunities such as the Dudgeon and Sheringham Shoal Extension projects.
The applicant's primary role will be to support operations at the Sheringham Shoal offshore wind farm. The position is based offshore on a Service Operations Vessel (SOV) and follows a 14-days-on/14-days-off rotation, working 12-hour shifts throughout each offshore deployment period.

As part of the United Infrastructure Group, we are a dynamic and innovative specialist engineering services, solutions and products provider focused on servicing our clients’ immediate and future needs.
